title: The Flock With No Leader
hook: A hundred thousand birds turn as one — and not one is in charge.
script: A hundred thousand birds turn at once, and not one of them is in charge. It looks impossible. A single shape twisting like it has a mind. But there is no mind, no leader, no plan. Each bird follows one tiny rule: watch only your nearest seven neighbors, and match them. That is it. Seven birds. None of them can see the whole flock. But that rule, copied across a hundred thousand bodies, builds a shape no single bird could ever picture. And when one edge turns, the turn races through the entire flock faster than any bird can react. Faster than their nerves should even allow. Scientists have measured it for years. They still cannot fully explain how the wave moves that fast.

first_frame.primary_object: A vast starling murmuration forming a single dark shape against an open sky
first_frame.contradiction: Thousands of separate birds moving as one solid object with no visible leader
first_frame.impact: The viewer instantly sees one living shape made of countless separate things.
